input: With the rapid development of evolutionary computation, large-scale multiobjective optimization has become a hot topic. It is worth noting that our method may potentially significantly outperform state-of-the-art algorithms, although we do not claim universal optimality.
must: Return revised English only when asked for text
Remove grand-opening, all active-research-area framing, and metadiscourse
Remove may significantly, defensive do-not-claim wording, and without-assuming universal disclaimers
Do not preserve the unsupported performance claim as an aim to outperform
State only the technical problem and research action supported by the input
must_not: Add baselines, numbers, citations, or results
Keep statistically significant without a test
Return a long diagnostic report by default
notes: Checks the default prose-first behavior and iterations 1-2 regressions.

input: Draft an introduction for an expensive multiobjective optimization paper using Gaussian-process-assisted differential evolution to reduce exact function evaluations. No baselines, numbers, or results are provided.
must: Write only what the supplied material supports
Use sparse-draft mode with at most 80 words of paper text
Do not infer candidate screening, training-set construction, model updates, archive rules, or budget allocation from the method name
Avoid invented citations, baselines, values, time costs, evaluation counts, outcomes, or a planned experimental study
List at most three missing details after the draft, prioritizing mechanism details needed for the method section
must_not: Use MISSING placeholders throughout the paper text
Generate a full multi-paragraph introduction from sparse notes
Fabricate a benchmark, statistical result, indicator plan, fixed budget, or paper-specific surrogate-management procedure
notes: Checks sparse drafting and the iteration-2 invention regression.

input: Audit: The proposed robust and scalable algorithm significantly outperforms all state-of-the-art optimizers and proves that it is optimal for expensive multiobjective optimization.
must: Identify proves/optimal as a theory-level overclaim
Identify all as an unsupported universal comparison
Require a defined statistical test for significantly
Require perturbation and dimension evidence for robust/scalable
Keep Revised text free of tested-problem, compared-baseline, and performance claims when no evidence is supplied
Keep verification commands, exit codes, and self-check notes out of Revised text
Limit the evidence-free fallback to the design target; do not add small budgets, Pareto-front approximation, or other goals
must_not: Return only a rewritten sentence without the requested audit
Treat robust or scalable as self-explanatory
notes: Checks explicit Audit mode and evidence-safe revision.

input: The surrogate-assisted algorithm is highly efficient because it converges in only 20 generations.
must: Avoid equating generations with expensive-evaluation efficiency
If efficiency is discussed, ask for or mark the need for exact FEs and model overhead; if efficiency is removed, no extra note is needed
Use neutral bounded wording if no cost data are provided
Preserve the exact count as exactly 20 generations or 20 generations; remove promotional only and do not change it to within 20 generations
must_not: Claim reduced expensive evaluations without evidence
notes: Checks EC-specific cost calibration and exact quantity qualifiers.

input: The algorithm improved Pareto front diversity in the decision space and convergence in the objective space.
must: Check whether the spatial attribution is technically consistent
Preserve convergence and diversity as distinct concepts
must_not: Treat objective value and fitness as interchangeable without explanation
